transcription.text: Hi. Just a quick second channel video, because a few people asked this one. So I thought I'd just demonstrate. I'm powering the Nixie tube from 170 volts here through the 22k resistor nominal that I was going to use, and people wanted to know what is the open voltage on the other pins, i.e. when they're switched off by the driver. And can you actually get away with a lower voltage driver, etc.?

Well, let's actually take one here and let's go around and measure some pins. What have we got? 49 volts. Hang on. Just got to be careful here. 24 volts. Quite some variation. 43. Whoops. 122. Ouch. 118. 69.

47, 123 odd. There you go. So there is quite a significant voltage on there. So 120, 223 volts there on a couple of pins. That means that just for this particular Nixitude, there's obviously great variation in this. So I could go and measure all eight. But yeah, and you're probably not going to get this from any of the other ones.

So that's the kind of open circuit voltage you need to withstand the voltage rating of your driver transistor or your driver transistor array or whatever you're going to use to actually drive this thing. So yeah, I'm afraid you can't get away with relying on the voltage drop of the Nixitude itself. So I hope that cleared that up. Catch you next time.
